    Two-sided operators on the algebra over the coordinate field #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.matrixImage_sandwich_independent {B : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_4} [Ring B] [Field K] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] [Fintype ι] (q : B →+* Matrix n n K) (b : Module.Basis ι K (Matrix n n K)) (hb : Set.range ⇑b ⊆ Set.range ⇑q) :
    LinearIndependent ↥(matrixCoefficientField q b) fun (p : ι × ι) => (AlgHom.mulLeftRight ↥(matrixCoefficientField q b) ↥(matrixImageAlgebra q b)) ((matrixImageBasis q b hb) p.1 ⊗ₜ[↥(matrixCoefficientField q b)] MulOpposite.op ((matrixImageBasis q b hb) p.2))

    The two-sided multiplication operators for a full matrix basis remain linearly independent over the field generated by the image coordinates.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.matrixImage_operator_expansion {B : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_4} [Ring B] [Field K] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] [Fintype ι] (q : B →+* Matrix n n K) (b : Module.Basis ι K (Matrix n n K)) (hb : Set.range ⇑b ⊆ Set.range ⇑q) (f : Module.End ↥(matrixCoefficientField q b) ↥(matrixImageAlgebra q b)) :
    ∃ (c : ι × ι → ↥(matrixCoefficientField q b)), ∀ (x : ↥(matrixImageAlgebra q b)), ∑ p : ι × ι, c p • ((matrixImageBasis q b hb) p.1 * x * (matrixImageBasis q b hb) p.2) = f x

    Every linear operator on the descended algebra is a linear combination of left and right multiplication by image basis elements.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.matrixImage_separating_multipliers {B : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_4} [Ring B] [Field K] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] [Fintype ι] (q : B →+* Matrix n n K) (b : Module.Basis ι K (Matrix n n K)) (hb : Set.range ⇑b ⊆ Set.range ⇑q) [DecidableEq ι] (l : ι) :
    ∃ (v : ι × ι → ↥(matrixImageAlgebra q b)), ∀ (i : ι), ∑ p : ι × ι, (matrixImageBasis q b hb) p.1 * (matrixImageBasis q b hb) i * v p = if i = l then 1 else 0

    Multipliers with left factors in the matrix image separate the basis vectors.
